instruction: A single nepenthes pitcher hanging from a curled tendril, rendered as flowing mirror-polished liquid metal. The trumpet body swells and ripples like poured mercury, its flared peristome lip rolling into a glossy torus and the lid frozen mid-drip above the mouth. Perfectly reflective surfaces smear the surroundings into stretched bands of silver and steel-blue.
